Folks — quick technical summary from initial triage:
- Timeline: kernel-selector rollout (v3.14.2 -> v3.15.0) started 07:20 UTC and completed ~07:25 UTC across us-west pools.
- Symptom: sustained drop in tokens/sec for gpt-*-quantized variants where the new selector chooses a different kernel path that disables a fused attention kernel on certain sequence lengths.
- Error rate: 502s correlate with an OOM fallback path on a small subset of servers under steady batching.
- Preliminary hypothesis: the selector change altered kernel choice heuristics for mid-length sequences (128-512 tokens) causing increased per-token runtime and worse KV cache reuse patterns.

Action items I am executing now (in parallel):
1) Rolling back kernel selector to v3.14.2 on the affected pool (starting now) — ETA 20 minutes. Tracking on JIRA-FF-6872.
2) Pulling perf dumps and token-rate histograms for the affected hosts and saving diffs (attaching kernel_selector_diff.patch / tps_drop_20270912.png).
3) If rollback is ineffective, we will force route FastFin traffic to a compatible model variant (non-quant) as a temporary mitigation.

Note: there is a canary policy but this change overloaded the selector heuristics for banks of GPUs we didn't catch in the canary due to a narrow traffic distribution. We need a postmortem and a stricter rollout gate.

-Markus

Adding next steps for the internal postmortem (draft):
- Root cause: kernel-selector heuristics change in v3.15 caused non-optimal kernel routing for mid-length sequences on quantized models -> increased per-token latency + KV cache inefficiency.
- Contributing factors: insufficient canary coverage for traffic distribution, missing metric that tracks kernel choice distribution per pool.
- Immediate mitigations implemented: rollback to v3.14.2 across affected pools; traffic pin for FastFin to pre-change selector; temporary routing to non-quant variants is on standby.
- Long-term: add rollout gate for kernel selection changes, expand canary matrix, add per-pool kernel-choice telemetry and auto-fallback if tokens/sec drops > 30% for >5 mins.

Hi Danielle — quick resolution note and next steps:

What happened: a kernel-selector heuristic change rolled in during your maintenance window and picked a slower execution path for mid-length sequences on quantized models. That reduced tokens/sec and increased p95/p99 for affected requests.

What we did: Markus rolled the selector back to the prior stable version within ~30 minutes of detection and pinned FastFin traffic to the pre-change selector while we completed verification. 502s dropped to baseline and token throughput recovered to ~95% of pre-incident volume.

Customer impact and remedy: we will propose a service credit for the affected window (07:20–09:10 UTC). Laura will follow up with a short executive summary and credit calculation.

Preventative steps: Rishi will deliver an RCA with the rollout gate and telemetry improvements; we'll add an automatic rollback trigger if tokens/sec drops >30% for >5 minutes on any reserved customer pool.

Please let us know a 30-minute slot tomorrow morning for a post-incident sync. Again — really sorry for the disruption. If you want immediate routing to non-quant variants while we complete the RCA, say the word and we'll activate it.
